what: When the top edge of a screen-covering video panel touches the top of the screen, the video plays from the start and scrolling is locked until it ends, loops once, or Skip is pressed (only once). A progress circle at bottom center (r48 · line 3) fills with the accent color by playback position, and while locked the Skip text rises in over .4s. Skip moves down to the panel’s bottom edge over 2s power2.inOut, and when you scroll back above the panel it stops and returns to the start. For intro pages that link sections with video interludes.

options.[data-fx-part=dock]: Progress circle + Skip button (child, optional) — inside Skip
options.dur: Scroll-down duration after Skip (sec), default 2 — 0 jumps straight there
options.ease: Curve for descending after Skip, default power2.inOut
options.lock: If false, scrolling is not stopped, and playback and progress are gentle
options.--fx-dock-ink: Progress circle baseline and Skip text color (CSS variable), default var(--kf-bg)

note: How to stop scrolling: lenis.stop() · start() if window.lenis exists, otherwise <html> sets overflow to hidden — it does not intercept touch. When locking and unlocking, the panel raises fx:lock and fx:unlock events, so anything else that uses smooth scrolling should listen for them and pause. In reduced-motion environments it does not lock and adds controls to the video
